correctness.rationale: For every projective isotropic direction ell, the affine coset-sum normal operator translates by all q points of ell. Fourier diagonalization gives q times the number of isotropic projective lines in xi^perp. An anisotropic frequency gives a nondegenerate (d-1)-form, and an isotropic frequency has a one-dimensional radical and (d-2)-dimensional nondegenerate quotient. Standard quadratic Gauss-sum zero counts with the correct Witt signs yield the claimed four multiplier branches and exact frequency multiplicities. d=3 has a zero stratum of size q(q-1)^2/2; d>=4 has positive minimum and the stated split/nonsplit dimension-four condition numbers. Orthogonal-group transitivity on projective null directions averages any direction weights and bounds the minimum Fourier eigenvalue, proving constant weights globally optimal. Independently enumerated all small p=3,5 fields in d=3,4, verifying multiplicities and both split types.
